correctness.rationale: A homomorphism induces a scalar c on the derived center and a linear A on V. The commutator identity imposes omega(Av,Aw)=c omega(v,w), and subtracting the group-law cocycle shows that the remaining central function ell is additive, hence linear over the prime field. If c≠0, A is invertible and so is the homomorphism. For c=0 the image of A is isotropic and the graph map has rank at most n+1; equality requires a Lagrangian W and ell nonzero on ker A. Surjectivity to W identifies A³=0 and ell A²=0 with B²=0 and ell vanishing on im B, where B=A|W. For rank s, choose im B⊂ker B and an isomorphism W/ker B→im B; this yields the two Gaussian binomials and |GL_s|. The extension count is the number of surjections from an n-dimensional complement to W/im B times p^(ns); ell choices are p^(2n-s)-p^n since im B⊂ker A. A square-zero linear map on the full 2n+1-dimensional group coordinate space has rank at most n. The positive s=0 term attains rank n+1 for cube zero and excludes index two. Direct independent enumeration for n=2,p=3 gives 138240 and 414720 by s=0,1, totalling 552960, and the n=1 formula specializes to 48 and 480 at p=3,5.
residual_risks: This is an odd-prime exponent-p group statement; the archived characteristic-two check is a Lie-algebra analogue only.
